result.title: PatientFlowSynth: Evaluating FHIR Agents with Matched Patient Charts
result.summary: Agents that search patient charts must classify claims from retrieved records, including cases with missing or conflicting evidence. In Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR), status fields can change how those records should be interpreted. PatientFlowSynth provides 18,000 tasks from 225 synthetic patients and 18 templates that hold the patient, question, and retrieval program fixed across chart variants representing four evidence states. Re-executing the program verifies each variant's reference answer, evidence sets, and search requirements. Strict success requires a completed response with correct labels and citations exactly matching an accepted evidence set retrieved during the episode. Where required, a tool response must also show a complete search at the specified scope. In a study using GPT-5.6 Luna and 225 synthetic patients (3,600 matched pairs), explicit Encounter-status guidance increased strict success from 40.7% to 51.3% (+10.6 percentage points; 95% patient-bootstrap confidence interval, 8.4 to 12.8). Among cases whose primary reference label was insufficient evidence, label agreement fell from 49.2% to 29.3%. A prespecified two-model replication reproduced both changes. Failed retrieval can mask interpretation errors by producing a correct insufficient-evidence label without examining the relevant records. Additional model comparisons showed that the benefit of guidance was model-dependent. Retrieval, citation, and classification should be evaluated separately.

AI.brief_summary: 构建基于 225 名合成 FHIR 患者、18,000 个任务的临床图表检索基准：固定问题与检索程序、只改变记录的证据状态，并重新执行检索程序核验参考标签与证据集；据此考察显式状态字段提示对严格成功率与「证据不足」判断的影响。
AI.relevance_reason: 其将检索、引用与分类分开评估，并指出检索失败会以「正确」的证据不足标签掩盖解释错误，可能为 LVR 中判断模型是否真正查看视觉证据、以及证据不足时的停止决策与评测设计提供借鉴，值得核查。
